es.summary: Conjunto de enzimas hepáticas que metabolizan la mayoría de los fármacos. Varias sustancias pueden inhibir o inducir su actividad, alterando los niveles séricos de los medicamentos.
key_points: CYP3A4 es la isoenzima más importante en la metabolización de fármacos
Inhibidores de CYP aumentan concentraciones y riesgo de toxicidad
Inductores de CYP reducen concentraciones y pueden disminuir eficacia
Las interacciones pueden afectar anticoagulantes, antiarrítmicos, benzodiacepinas, entre otros

mechanism: Oxida y elimina fármacos mediante reacciones de hidroxilación
Presente principalmente en el retículo endoplásmico del hepatocito
CYP3A4 metaboliza ≈50% de los fármacos clínicos
interactions: Inhibidores de CYP3A4: eritromicina, claritromicina, azoles (fluconazol, itraconazol)
Inductores de CYP3A4: rifampicina, carbamazepina, hierba de San Juan
Aumento del INR con warfarina cuando se combina con inhibidores de CYP
Disminución de niveles de digoxina con inductores de CYP
nursing_care: Revisar lista de medicamentos antes de administrar un nuevo fármaco
Obtener y registrar niveles séricos (p. ej., INR, niveles de digoxina)
Retener la dosis si el paciente presenta signos de toxicidad
Notificar al médico si se identifican interacciones potenciales
patient_teaching: Informar que algunos antibióticos y antifúngicos pueden alterar la acción de otros medicamentos
Evitar el consumo de pomelo o jugo de pomelo sin consultar al profesional
Reportar cualquier sangrado inusual o cambios en la presión arterial

outcomes: Riesgo de sangrado: No presentar hemorragias durante la hospitalización
Riesgo de sangrado: INR dentro del rango terapéutico especificado

interventions.action: Revisar la orden médica y la lista de medicamentos para identificar inhibidores o inductores de CYP
interventions.rationale: Previene interacciones que puedan elevar o disminuir niveles de fármacos críticos

interventions.action: Obtener y registrar niveles de INR y otros parámetros de coagulación según indicación
interventions.rationale: Permite detectar desviaciones tempranas del rango terapéutico

interventions.action: Educar al paciente sobre los signos de sangrado y la importancia de reportarlos inmediatamente
interventions.rationale: Facilita la detección precoz de hemorragias

interventions.action: Coordinar con el farmacéutico para ajustar dosis cuando se añaden o retiran inhibidores/inductores
interventions.rationale: Asegura que la terapia mantenga su efectividad y seguridad

interventions.action: Monitorear signos vitales y hemograma completo cada 24‑48 h según criterio clínico
interventions.rationale: Detecta cambios en la hemostasia y posibles efectos adversos

en.summary: A group of hepatic enzymes that metabolize most drugs. Various substances can inhibit or induce their activity, altering serum drug levels.
key_points: CYP3A4 is the most important isoenzyme in drug metabolism
CYP inhibitors increase concentrations and risk of toxicity
CYP inducers reduce concentrations and may decrease efficacy
Interactions can affect anticoagulants, antiarrhythmics, benzodiazepines, among others

mechanism: Oxidizes and eliminates drugs via hydroxylation reactions
Primarily located in the endoplasmic reticulum of hepatocytes
interactions: CYP3A4 inhibitors: erythromycin, clarithromycin, azoles (fluconazole, itraconazole)
CYP3A4 inducers: rifampin, carbamazepine, St. John’s wort
Increased INR with warfarin when combined with CYP inhibitors
Reduced digoxin levels with CYP inducers
nursing_care: Review medication list before administering a new drug
Obtain and record serum levels (e.g., INR, digoxin levels)
Hold the dose if the patient shows signs of toxicity
Notify the physician if potential interactions are identified
patient_teaching: Inform that some antibiotics and antifungals can alter the action of other medications
Avoid consuming grapefruit or grapefruit juice without consulting a professional
Report any unusual bleeding or changes in blood pressure

outcomes: Risk of bleeding: No hemorrhages during hospitalization
Risk of bleeding: INR within specified therapeutic range

interventions.action: Review the medical order and medication list to identify CYP inhibitors or inducers
interventions.rationale: Prevents interactions that may raise or lower critical drug levels

interventions.action: Obtain and record INR and other coagulation parameters as indicated
interventions.rationale: Allows early detection of deviations from the therapeutic range

interventions.action: Educate the patient about bleeding signs and the importance of reporting them immediately
Coordinate with the pharmacist to adjust doses when inhibitors/inducers are added or removed
interventions.rationale: Ensures therapy remains effective and safe

interventions.action: Monitor vital signs and complete blood count every 24‑48 h as clinically indicated
interventions.rationale: Detects changes in hemostasis and potential adverse effects

key_points.1.quote: Affected medications will have higher levels in the body and increase the risk for drug toxicity.

sections.nursing_care.0.quote: For clients taking macrolides, always review their medication list for medications metabolized by CYP3A4.

sections.patient_teaching.0.quote: Some oral and intravenously administered azole antifungals are strong inhibitors of CYP3A4, which can affect many medications.

sections.patient_teaching.1.quote: Recommended to consult a pharmacist for evaluation of drug interactions with warfarin
